summary:
Scope: the coord engine's workspace commands take an exclusive configuration lock without waiting (WorkspaceTelemetryApplication): a second caller gets configuration-busy instead of blocking. A user timer that drains the same association every few minutes therefore overlaps a foreground loop that also captures and drains.

Observed failure: the loop's drain returned configuration-busy while the timer's own drain had already applied the loop's ready batch. The loop stopped on its non-zero exit, correctly, but one applied batch was missing from its ledger. Do not retry blindly and do not edit the ledger: verify by hand that receiver receipts equal recorded plus one, the Claude fact count grew by at most one batch (24), the outcome file for the next batch id is applied, no ready file or pending intent remains and no receipt was rejected, then record that single round through a reconcile step that refuses to act unless every check passes. A read-only monitoring query against the live sqlite file can also fail with database is locked while the Host writes; retry a small bounded number of times and treat persistent failure as a stop.

Resolution that held without pausing the installed path: a scheduling-only guard before each round that waits until the drain service is idle and the next timer tick is more than about 55 s away, bounded at 15 minutes, logging any wait. It added waits of under a minute about once per timer period and no overlap in the remaining rounds. Pausing the timer was not needed and would have changed the installed path under test. The timer also remains able to drain the loop's batch, so ledger reconciliation stays the recovery for any future overlap.
title: A unattended drain timer and a foreground capture loop contend on the configuration lock; guard the schedule and reconcile an applied-but-unrecorded batch
